title: How an Elevator Works in 60 Seconds 🛗⬆️ #shorts
description:
In most tall buildings, the elevator motor barely lifts you. The car hangs from steel ropes looped over a grooved wheel, and a hidden counterweight on the other side, about the car's weight plus 40% of its load, does most of the work. A speed governor can trip safety brakes that clamp the rails. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#elevator #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: In most tall buildings, the elevator motor *barely lifts you*. A hidden partner does most of the work.

steps.label: Ropes
steps.text: The car hangs from several *steel ropes*, looped over a grooved wheel called a *sheave*.

steps.label: Counterweight
steps.text: On the other side hangs a *counterweight*. It weighs the car, plus about 40 percent of a full load.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: So the *motor* only moves the difference. It turns the sheave, and *friction* grips the ropes.

steps.label: Rails
steps.text: As the car rises, the counterweight drops. Both glide on steel *guide rails*.

steps.label: Safety
steps.text: If the car ever goes too fast, a *governor* trips *safety brakes* that clamp onto the rails.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Ropes, weight, *grip*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
